extracted.intended_audience: AI/ML and HCI researchers and developers, defense program managers, and practitioners interested in explainable AI
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, building, and evaluating machine-learning systems that produce human-understandable explanations while retaining high predictive performance; integrating ML models with human-computer interfaces and human-subject evaluation. Focus includes classification and reinforcement-learning challenge problems relevant to defense operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce more explainable models while maintaining high learning performance
rubrics_metrics.description: The XAI program aims to create a suite of machine learning techniques that: Produce more explainable models, while maintaining a high level of learning performance (prediction accuracy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should explicitly address the performance-versus-explainability trade space — methods must improve explainability without unacceptable loss in prediction accuracy. The program strategy pursues a variety of techniques to provide design options covering this trade space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enable human users to understand, appropriately trust, and effectively manage AI partners
rubrics_metrics.description: Enable human users to understand, appropriately trust, and effectively manage the emerging generation of artificially intelligent partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanations should support human comprehension, calibrated trust, and effective control/management of autonomous systems; evaluation should measure user understanding and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Models must explain their rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: New machine-learning systems will have the ability to explain their rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanations should communicate why a model made a particular decision or prediction in a way that is meaningful to end users (possibly via HCI techniques and dialogue).

rubrics_metrics.name: Models must characterize their strengths and weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: New machine-learning systems will have the ability to ... characterize their strengths and weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems should report limitations, failure modes, confidence, and contexts in which outputs are reliable or not, to help users judge applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Models must convey understanding of future behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: New machine-learning systems will have the ability to ... convey an understanding of how they will behave in the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predictions about future behavior or policy outcomes should be presented so users can anticipate system actions and consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate ML models with state-of-the-art HCI for understandable explanation dialogues
rubrics_metrics.description: These models will be combined with state-of-the-art human-computer interface techniques capable of translating models into understandable and useful explanation dialogues for the end user.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work must include end-user-facing explanation modalities (e.g., dialogues, visualizations), and engineering to translate model internals into usable explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursue a portfolio of methods covering the performance-vs-explainability trade space
rubrics_metrics.description: Our strategy is to pursue a variety of techniques in order to generate a portfolio of methods that will provide future developers with a range of design options covering the performance-versus-explainability trade space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should explore diverse methodological approaches rather than a single solution, enabling selection among alternatives depending on operational needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target challenge problems in classification and decision-policy construction
rubrics_metrics.description: The XAI program is focused on the development of multiple systems by addressing challenge problems in two areas: (1) machine learning problems to classify events of interest in heterogeneous, multimedia data; and (2) machine learning problems to construct decision policies for an autonomous system to perform a variety of simulated missions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chosen problem domains are intended to represent the intersection of classification and reinforcement-learning approaches and map to DoD operational areas (intelligence analysis and autonomous systems). Proposals/evaluations should align with these challenge problem types or justify domain relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate psychology of explanation and human-subject evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition, researchers are examining the psychology of explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research should include cognitive/psychological considerations of what constitutes a good explanation for humans, and empirically evaluate explanations with users (pilot studies, user experiments) to assess effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continual testing and phased system evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: XAI research prototypes are tested and continually evaluated throughout the course of the program. ... Full Phase 1 system evaluations are expected in November 2018.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs should plan iterative development with ongoing evaluation checkpoints, pilot studies early, then full system evaluations per program phases; evaluation metrics should track both model performance and explanation utility for users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliver a toolkit library of ML and HCI software modules suitable for transition
rubrics_metrics.description: At the end of the program, the final delivery will be a toolkit library consisting of machine learning and human-computer interface software modules that could be used to develop future explainable AI systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final artifacts should be modular, reusable, combine ML and HCI components, and be suitable for further refinement and transition into defense or commercial applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance toward third-wave AI: contextual understanding and evolving explanatory models
rubrics_metrics.description: XAI is ... expected to enable 'third-wave AI systems', where machines understand the context and environment in which they operate, and over time build underlying explanatory models that allow them to characterize real world phenomena.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research should aim for systems that capture contextual knowledge and can incrementally build or refine explanations over time rather than providing only static post-hoc justifications.
